Dixon, Gary E.; Crookston, Nicholas L. 2016. Model Structure of the Forest Vegetation Simulator. Internal Rep. Fort Collins, CO: U. S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service, Forest Management Service Center. 128p. (Revised: June 29, 2016)

This document describes basic model structure for the Forest Vegetation Simulator (FVS) computer software. This guide explains model flow, logic considerations, subcomponents, and subroutines for the base model including the regeneration establishment and event monitor extensions. It also discusses how to accomplish common programming tasks associated with code maintenance or enhancement. This document is meant to serve as an initial reference for people involved with design or modification of the FVS model computer code.

Keywords: Forest Vegetation Simulator, forest management, simulation models, resource management.

## About the Authors {-}

Gary E. Dixon (retired) is a biometrician and served as the Forest Vegetation Simulator Group leader at the Forest Service’s Washington Office Forest Management Service Center in Fort Collins, Colorado. Dr. Dixon received his B.S. (1973), M.S. (1974), and Ph.D. (1977) in forest biometrics at Colorado State University. He has worked on the development of tree growth models throughout most of his career. He joined the Forest Management Staff in 1982 and has worked with the model now known as the Forest Vegetation Simulator since that time. He retired from the Forest Service in 2008 but still actively participates in FVS development.

Nicholas L. Crookston (retired) was an operations research analyst and worked at the Forest Service’s Rocky Mountain Research Station, Forestry Sciences Laboratory in Moscow, Idaho. He has participated in the development of FVS from about 1977 to the present time. Dr. Crookston received his B.S. (1973) in botany at Weber State University, M.S. (1977) and Honorary Doctorate of Natural Resources (2015) from the University of Idaho. He retired from the Forest Service in 2015 but still actively participates in FVS development.

We would like to thank all those people that contributed to the development, testing, and support of the FVS software system. We would also like to thank the many FVS users who have provided feedback and suggested model improvements over the years.

## About this Guide {-}

This document is meant to serve as a technical guide to the FVS model and document program flow and programming considerations of the model. As such it is intended for people involved with FVS model development and code modification. This document a technical supplement to the two FVS user’s guides referenced in the following section.

## How to use this Guide {-}

Anyone reading this document should also have “Essential FVS: A user’s guide to the Forest Vegetation Simulator” and the “Keyword Reference Guide for the Forest Vegetation Simulator” at hand. These can be downloaded from the Forest Management Service Center’s web site. Any references in this document to the “EFVS Guide” or “Keyword Guide” are referencing these documents. When a keyword record name is mentioned in this document, it should be looked up in the keyword guide for a detailed discussion of the parameter fields and other explanatory notes.

Developers should also obtain the FVS overview document for the variant pertaining to their geographic area from the same web site. With these three documents, plus this one, model developers should have a good start towards understanding the FVS model structure.

Users wanting to interface with FVS using the Suppose graphical user interface should obtain that software along with the “exercise guide” pertaining to their geographic area. These products are also available from the FMSC web site. A new online tool for running FVS, called FVSOnline, is now available.  FVSOnline is intended to replace Suppose and takes advantage of some newer programming constructs documented in this document. FVSOnline can also be run on a local machine.



# Introduction

The Forest Vegetation Simulator (FVS) is a model used for predicting forest stand dynamics that is used extensively in the United States. User’s guides exist for those people interested in running their data through FVS (Dixon 2002, VanDyck and Smith-Mateja 2000) and model relationships specific to geographic variants are presented in the various variant overview guides (e.g. Keyser and Dixon 2008). However, formal technical documentation of the programming flow and logic has not been previously available in a consolidated place. This document provides this type of documentation for the FVS base model including the regeneration establishment and event monitor extensions. Some mention will be made of other FVS extensions, such as the database extension, where appropriate.

Sections 2.0 through 2.2 of this document discuss general FVS structure and programming considerations. Sections 3.0 through 5.2 are generally arranged in the order that FVS processes a stand. Sections 6.0 through 8.0, and section 10.0, are devoted entirely to describing the program flow and logic in a particular section of the FVS code, or a particular FVS feature. Section 9.0 describes structural differences in the two ORGANON-FVS variants.

# General Flow Overview

The general processing sequence for FVS is shown in figure 2-1 and discussed in section 3.4 of the EFVS guide. Each of the major task groupings shown in this processing sequence will be further broken down in following sections.

FVS can process a single stand in one model run or many stands in one model run. When running FVS there are two processing modes, serial or parallel. A serial run occurs when each stand is processed to completion before the next stand starts. A parallel run occurs when all the stands are processed up to a common stopping year, typically before the end of the projection, and then the program is stopped. Other processes can then be run that can include the creation of information FVS can use when a simulation is resumed. Once the simulation resumes, all the stands are processed up to the next common stopping point or the end of the projection.

Prior to about 2012, running stands in the parallel mode required the use of a separate version of FVS that included the Parallel Processing Extension (PPE, Crookston and Stage, 1991).  However, given the complexity of that program and its lack of use, The PPE was removed and FVS was modified to include the ability to stop and restart itself. This will be discussed in further detail in section 8.0.

Most of this document is devoted to explaining the processing sequence for a single stand serial model run. A multiple stand serial model run follows the same processing sequence as a single stand serial model run, repeated for each stand. A parallel model run follows virtually the same flow as its serial counterpart for each stand in the projection initialization, projection cycling, and projection summarization phases. Details on how this is accomplished are covered in section 8.0.

The general processing flow for a single stand serial model run can be broken down into three phases. The projection initialization phase gets the stand ready to run; the projection cycling phase projects the stand through time; and the projection summarization phase produces the output reports.

## Detailed Input and Output Array Specifications {-}

The following tables summarize the major FVS subroutines and the arrays they use:

### Subroutine Summary Tables {-}

#### Main Control Flow Functions {-}

```{r main-control-table, echo=FALSE}
main_control <- data.frame(
  Function = c("FVS", "INITRE", "TREGRO"),
  Purpose = c(
    "Main simulation driver that orchestrates the entire projection cycle",
    "Initializes prognosis run, processes keywords and options",
    "Main tree growth routine called each cycle"
  ),
  Input_Arrays = c(
    "PRGPRM.F77, ARRAYS.F77, PLOT.F77, CONTRL.F77, OUTCOM.F77, PDEN.F77, ECON.F77, WORKCM.F77",
    "All major common blocks, keyword file data, stand parameters",
    "PRGPRM.F77, CONTRL.F77, Cycle number (ICYC)"
  ),
  Output = c(
    "IRTNCD (error/status code)",
    "Initialized stand variables, control flags",
    "Calls GRINCR and GRADD to compute increments"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

kable(main_control,
      col.names = c("Function Name", "Purpose", "Input Arrays", "Output"),
      caption = "Main Control Flow Functions",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

#### Growth and Mortality Processing Functions {-}

```{r growth-mort-table, echo=FALSE}
growth_mort <- data.frame(
  Function = c("GRINCR", "GRADD", "UPDATE", "MORTS"),
  Purpose = c(
    "Computes growth and mortality for each tree record",
    "Updates tree descriptions and adds increments",
    "Adds growth increment, deducts mortality, computes volumes",
    "Calculates tree mortality rates (variant-specific)"
  ),
  Input_Arrays = c(
    "PLOT.F77, ARRAYS.F77, CONTRL.F77, PDEN.F77; DBH(), HT(), ISP(), DG(), HTG()",
    "ARRAYS.F77, COEFFS.F77, CONTRL.F77; DG(), HTG(), DBH(), HT(), PROB()",
    "ARRAYS.F77, COEFFS.F77, CONTRL.F77; HT(), HTG(), DBH(), DG(), WK2(), IMC()",
    "Variant-specific common blocks; Stand density (BA, SDI, CCF), tree attributes"
  ),
  Output = c(
    "DG() - diameter growth/year; HTG() - height growth; WK2() - mortality (TPA)",
    "Updated DBH(), HT(), scaled DG() to cycle length",
    "Updated HT(), DBH(), PROB(); WK6() - mortality volume; OMORT() - mortality summary",
    "WK2() - mortality (trees/acre); IMC() - mortality class"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

kable(growth_mort,
      col.names = c("Function Name", "Purpose", "Input Arrays", "Output"),
      caption = "Growth and Mortality Processing Functions",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

#### Stand Density and Statistics Functions {-}

```{r density-stats-table, echo=FALSE}
density_stats <- data.frame(
  Function = c("DENSE", "NOTRE", "SETUP", "STATS"),
  Purpose = c(
    "Calculates stand density statistics",
    "Calculates trees per acre from sampling design",
    "Sets up index pointers for species-ordered sort",
    "Computes statistical description of input data"
  ),
  Input_Arrays = c(
    "PLOT.F77, ARRAYS.F77; DBH(), HT(), PROB(), ISP(), ICR(), DG()",
    "PRGPRM.F77, ARRAYS.F77; PROB(), DBH(), BAF, FPA, BRK, PI",
    "PRGPRM.F77, ARRAYS.F77; IREF(), KOUNT(), IBEGIN(), IND2(), IREC1",
    "ARRAYS.F77, CONTRL.F77; DBH(), PROB(), CFV(), BFV(), ISP(), PI, ALPHA"
  ),
  Output = c(
    "BA, TPROB, RELDEN (CCF), RMSQD (QMD), AVH, PCT(), RELDSP()",
    "PROB() - trees/acre based on plot design",
    "IND1() - species-ordered indices; ISCT(,1-2) - first/last by species; ITRN",
    "Stand statistics (mean, std dev, CV, confidence intervals); Species summaries"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

kable(density_stats,
      col.names = c("Function Name", "Purpose", "Input Arrays", "Output"),
      caption = "Stand Density and Statistics Functions",
      booktabs = TRUE) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE) %>%
  column_spec(1, bold = TRUE)
```

## Processing Sequence Diagrams {-}

This section provides detailed flowcharts and sequence diagrams for major FVS processing workflows.

### Overall FVS Execution Sequence {-}

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         MAIN PROGRAM                            │
│                                                                 │
│  1. Initialize runtime environment                             │
│  2. Process command-line arguments                             │
│  3. Open keyword file                                          │
└────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      SUBROUTINE FVS                             │
│                   (Main Simulation Driver)                      │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  CYCLE = 0: Initialization Phase                        │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  │  ┌────────────────────┐                                 │  │
│  │  │   INITRE           │  Initialize projection         │  │
│  │  │   ├─ KEYSET        │  Read keywords                  │  │
│  │  │   ├─ RDPSRT        │  Read stand/tree data          │  │
│  │  │   ├─ NOTRE         │  Calculate TPA                 │  │
│  │  │   ├─ SETUP         │  Sort/index trees              │  │
│  │  │   ├─ DENSE         │  Calculate density             │  │
│  │  │   ├─ CRATET        │  Calibrate models              │  │
│  │  │   └─ STATS         │  Inventory statistics          │  │
│  │  └────────────────────┘                                 │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  CYCLES 1 to NCYC: Growth Projection Phase              │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  │  DO ICYC = 1, NCYC                                       │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   CUTS (vbase)     │  Before-growth thinning      │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │              ▼                                           │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   EVMON (1st call) │  Event monitor (pre-growth)  │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │              ▼                                           │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   TREGRO           │  Tree growth routine         │  │
│  │    │   ├─ GRINCR        │    Compute DG, HTG, MORT     │  │
│  │    │   └─ GRADD         │    Add increments            │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │              ▼                                           │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   CUTS (vbase)     │  After-growth thinning       │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │              ▼                                           │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   EVMON (2nd call) │  Event monitor (post-growth) │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │              ▼                                           │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   ESINIT/ESTAB     │  Regeneration establishment  │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │              ▼                                           │  │
│  │    ┌────────────────────┐                               │  │
│  │    │   SUMARY           │  Write summary output        │  │
│  │    └────────────────────┘                               │  │
│  │              │                                           │  │
│  │  END DO (next cycle)                                     │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                                                 │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  Post-Processing Phase                                   │  │
│  │                                                          │  │
│  │  ┌────────────────────┐                                 │  │
│  │  │   Close output     │  Close all output files        │  │
│  │  │   files            │                                 │  │
│  │  └────────────────────┘                                 │  │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Initialization Phase Detail (Cycle 0) {-}

```
INITRE - Initialization and Setup
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Start INITRE
     │
     ├──> KEYSET ────> Read and validate all keyword records
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> Extension keywords (FIRE, ECON, etc.)
     │                  ├─> Management keywords (THIN, PLANT, etc.)
     │                  └─> Output control keywords
     │
     ├──> RDPSRT ───┬─> Read tree records (FIA format or other)
     │              │
     │              └─> Sort by species and diameter
     │
     ├──> NOTRE ────> Calculate trees per acre (PROB array)
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> Variable radius: PROB = 43560/(BAF*PI)
     │                  └─> Fixed area: PROB = trees/plot_area
     │
     ├──> SETUP ────> Create species-ordered indices
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> Build IND1() array (species order)
     │                  ├─> Build ISCT(,1) and ISCT(,2) pointers
     │                  └─> Count trees by species
     │
     ├──> DENSE ────> Calculate stand density metrics
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> BA = Σ(0.005454*DBH²*PROB)
     │                  ├─> CCF = Σ(crown_area*PROB/43560)
     │                  ├─> SDI = TPROB*(QMD/10)^1.605
     │                  └─> AVH = height of 40 largest trees/acre
     │
     ├──> CCFCAL ───> Compute crown widths and CCF
     │
     ├──> CRATET ───> Calibration and dubbing
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> Dub missing heights (HTCALC)
     │                  ├─> Dub missing crown ratios (CROWN)
     │                  ├─> Estimate site index if needed
     │                  ├─> Calibrate DG model (DGCAL)
     │                  ├─> Calibrate HT model (HTCAL)
     │                  └─> Calibrate mortality model (if applicable)
     │
     ├──> VOLS ─────> Calculate initial volumes
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> CFV() - Total cubic foot
     │                  ├─> MCFV() - Merchantable cubic
     │                  └─> BFV() - Board foot (Scribner)
     │
     ├──> STATS ────> Compute inventory statistics
     │                  │
     │                  ├─> Mean, std dev by plot
     │                  ├─> Confidence intervals
     │                  └─> Sampling error
     │
     └──> SUMARY ───> Write initial conditions report

Return from INITRE
```

### Growth Cycle Processing Detail {-}

```
TREGRO - Tree Growth for One Cycle
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Start TREGRO (ICYC = current cycle number)                  │
└────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
        ┌─────────────────┐
        │    GRINCR       │ Compute growth and mortality
        └────────┬────────┘
                 │
       ┌─────────┴─────────┐
       │                   │
       ▼                   ▼
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│  DGDRIV     │     │   HTGF      │ Height growth
│  │          │     │  (variant)  │
│  ├─ DGF     │     └─────────────┘
│  │  (var)   │            │
│  │          │            │
│  └─ DGCAL   │            │
│     (calib) │            │
└──────┬──────┘            │
       │                   │
       │      ┌────────────┘
       │      │
       ▼      ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│  Per-tree diameter growth:      │
│  DG(I) = f(DBH, BA, CCF,        │
│            site, species, ...)  │
│                                 │
│  Per-tree height growth:        │
│  HTG(I) = f(HT, DBH, DG,        │
│             site, species)      │
└──────────────┬──────────────────┘
               │
               ▼
        ┌─────────────┐
        │   REGENT    │ Small tree growth (DBH < 3")
        │  (variant)  │
        └──────┬──────┘
               │
               ▼
        ┌─────────────┐
        │    MORTS    │ Mortality calculation
        │  (variant)  │
        │             │
        │  WK2(I) =   │ Mortality TPA per tree
        │    f(DBH,   │
        │      CR,    │
        │      BA,    │
        │      SDI)   │
        └──────┬──────┘
               │
               ▼
        ┌─────────────┐
        │   FFERT     │ Fertilizer response (if active)
        └──────┬──────┘
               │
Return from GRINCR
               │
               ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        GRADD                                 │
│            Add growth and apply mortality                    │
└────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
             │
             ├──> Scale DG to cycle length: DG = DG * FINT
             │
             ├──> Extension Models (if active)
             │    │
             │    ├─> MPBCUP  (Mountain Pine Beetle)
             │    ├─> DFBDRV  (Douglas-fir Beetle)
             │    ├─> BWECUP  (Western Spruce Budworm)
             │    ├─> TMCOUP  (Tussock Moth)
             │    ├─> FMMAIN  (Fire & Fuels Extension)
             │    ├─> BRTREG  (Bark Beetle)
             │    └─> RDTREG  (Root Disease)
             │
             ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │   UPDATE    │ Update tree attributes
      └──────┬──────┘
             │
             ├──> Add height growth:
             │    HT(I) = HT(I) + HTG(I)
             │
             ├──> Add diameter growth:
             │    DBH(I) = DBH(I) + DG(I)
             │
             ├──> Subtract mortality:
             │    PROB(I) = PROB(I) - WK2(I)
             │
             ├──> Call VOLS to recalculate volumes
             │    │
             │    ├─> CFV(I)  - Total cubic
             │    ├─> MCFV(I) - Merch cubic
             │    └─> BFV(I)  - Board foot
             │
             ├──> Accumulate mortality to OMORT(,,)
             │
             └──> Update stand summaries

Return from GRADD
             │
             ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │   CROWN     │ Update crown dimensions
      └──────┬──────┘
             │
             ├──> Predict crown ratio change
             ├──> Update ICR() array
             │
             ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │  CWIDTH     │ Update crown width
      └──────┬──────┘
             │
             ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │   DENSE     │ Recalculate stand density
      └──────┬──────┘
             │
             └──> Update BA, TPROB, CCF, SDI, QMD, AVH

Return from TREGRO
```

### Thinning Processing Sequence {-}

```
CUTS - Thinning and Removal Processing
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Start CUTS (vbase)
     │
     ├──> Check for scheduled thinning in current year
     │    │
     │    └──> If no thinning: RETURN
     │
     ▼
Determine thinning type and target:
     │
     ├──> THINBTA: Thin from Below to Target BA
     ├──> THINATA: Thin from Above to Target BA
     ├──> THINSDI: Thin to Target SDI
     ├──> THINCCF: Thin to Target CCF
     ├──> THINTPA: Thin to Target TPA
     └──> THINDBH: Diameter Limit Cut

For each thinning activity:
     │
     ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1. Calculate Current Stand Density                        │
│     │                                                       │
│     ├─> BA_current                                        │
│     ├─> SDI_current                                       │
│     ├─> CCF_current                                       │
│     └─> TPA_current                                       │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  2. Determine Removal Amount                               │
│     │                                                       │
│     └─> BA_to_remove = BA_current - BA_target             │
│                                                            │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  3. Rank Trees for Removal                                 │
│     │                                                       │
│     ├─> Thin from Below: Sort by PCT (smallest first)     │
│     ├─> Thin from Above: Sort by PCT (largest first)      │
│     └─> Apply species preferences if specified            │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  4. Select Trees for Removal                               │
│     │                                                       │
│     │  DO I = 1, ITRN (in removal order)                  │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    ├─> Calculate tree BA contribution               │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    ├─> If within diameter limits AND                │
│     │    │    species matches criteria:                   │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    │    ├─> WK3(I) = PROB(I) * efficiency          │
│     │    │    │    (trees removed)                        │
│     │    │    │                                           │
│     │    │    ├─> BA_removed += 0.005454*DBH²*WK3(I)     │
│     │    │    │                                           │
│     │    │    └─> If BA_removed >= BA_to_remove:         │
│     │    │         EXIT loop                             │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │  END DO                                              │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  5. Calculate Removed Volumes                              │
│     │                                                       │
│     │  DO I = 1, ITRN                                      │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    ├─> WK4(I) = CFV(I) * WK3(I) / PROB(I)          │
│     │    │    (cubic feet removed)                        │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    ├─> WK5(I) = MCFV(I) * WK3(I) / PROB(I)         │
│     │    │    (merch cubic removed)                       │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    └─> WK6(I) = BFV(I) * WK3(I) / PROB(I)          │
│     │         (board feet removed)                        │
│     │  END DO                                              │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  6. Update Tree List                                       │
│     │                                                       │
│     │  DO I = 1, ITRN                                      │
│     │    │                                                 │
│     │    └─> PROB(I) = PROB(I) - WK3(I)                  │
│     │         (reduce TPA by removal amount)              │
│     │  END DO                                              │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  7. Accumulate Removal Statistics                         │
│     │                                                       │
│     ├─> Update ONTREM(,,) by species/size class           │
│     ├─> Update removal summaries                          │
│     └─> Call DBSCUTS (if database output active)         │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │   DENSE     │ Recalculate density after cutting
      └──────┬──────┘
             │
             └──> Update BA, TPROB, CCF, SDI

Return from CUTS
```

### Stand Density Calculation Sequence {-}

```
DENSE - Stand Density and Structure Calculation
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Start DENSE
     │
     ▼
Initialize accumulators:
     │
     ├─> BA_total = 0
     ├─> TPA_total = 0
     ├─> BA_by_species() = 0
     ├─> Sum_DBH2_TPA = 0
     └─> Top_trees_list() = empty

     │
     ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Loop through all tree records (I = 1 to ITRN)             │
│                                                            │
│  For each tree with PROB(I) > 0:                          │
│    │                                                       │
│    ├─> BA_i = 0.005454 * DBH(I)² * PROB(I)              │
│    │                                                       │
│    ├─> BA_total = BA_total + BA_i                        │
│    │                                                       │
│    ├─> TPA_total = TPA_total + PROB(I)                   │
│    │                                                       │
│    ├─> BA_by_species(ISP(I)) += BA_i                     │
│    │                                                       │
│    ├─> Sum_DBH2_TPA += DBH(I)² * PROB(I)                 │
│    │                                                       │
│    └─> Add to top_trees_list if HT(I) large enough       │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Calculate Summary Statistics                              │
│                                                            │
│  BA = BA_total (basal area, sq ft/ac)                     │
│                                                            │
│  TPROB = TPA_total (trees per acre)                       │
│                                                            │
│  RMSQD = SQRT(Sum_DBH2_TPA / TPA_total)                   │
│          (quadratic mean diameter)                        │
│                                                            │
│  AVH = Average of 40 largest trees/ac from                │
│        top_trees_list sorted by height                    │
│        (Avg Ht of dominants)                              │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
      ┌─────────────┐
      │   CCFCAL    │ Calculate Crown Competition Factor
      └──────┬──────┘
             │
             ├─> For each tree:
             │   Crown_area = f(DBH, HT, CR, species)
             │   CCF_i = Crown_area * PROB(I) / 43560
             │
             ├─> RELDEN = Σ CCF_i (total CCF)
             │
             └─> RELDSP(ISP) = CCF by species

             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Calculate Stand Density Index (SDI)                       │
│                                                            │
│  SDI = TPA_total * (RMSQD / 10)^1.605                     │
│        (Reineke 1933)                                      │
│                                                            │
│  Relative Density = SDI / SDIMAX(species)                 │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Calculate Percentile Distribution                         │
│                                                            │
│  1. Sort trees by DBH (largest to smallest) → IND2()      │
│                                                            │
│  2. For each tree I in sorted order:                      │
│     │                                                      │
│     ├─> Cumulative_BA += BA_i                            │
│     │                                                      │
│     └─> PCT(I) = 100 * Cumulative_BA / BA_total          │
│          (percentile in BA distribution)                  │
└────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
Optional: Backdate one year if LBKDEN = TRUE
     │
     └─> DBH_backdated = DBH - DG
          Recalculate all metrics with backdated DBH

Return from DENSE with:
     │
     ├─> BA (basal area)
     ├─> TPROB (trees/acre)
     ├─> RELDEN (CCF)
     ├─> RMSQD (QMD)
     ├─> AVH (avg height of dominants)
     ├─> SDI (stand density index)
     ├─> PCT() (percentiles)
     └─> RELDSP() (CCF by species)
```


## Overall Model Design and Control

This section describes some underlying concepts behind FVS structure and discusses the routines involved in overall program control.

### Programming Language, Comments, and Debugging

FVS code has evolved through time as computer systems and languages have changed. FVS was developed in FORTRAN IV, upgraded in places to FORTRAN V, ultimately converted to FORTRAN 77, and currently contains FORTRAN 90, 95, and 2003 constructs. The code is continually upgraded and older code constructs eliminated as time permits. FVS is fully compatible with a FORTRAN compiler that supports the 2003 standard. The code was originally designed to run on a mainframe computer system and was changed to also run on personal computer (PC) systems around 1985. Mainframe usage has dwindled and many applications of FVS are now run on a PC. However, there are many uses of FVS and some of them are accomplished on large servers where hundreds of thousands of runs are done. The FVS code is supported on a range of computer systems, including Windows, Linux-based systems, and Unix-based systems like MAC OSX. Building FVS from source code can be done using various approaches. These are documented in wiki pages at url:https://sourceforge.net/p/open-fvs/wiki/browse_pages/.

FVS code contains many comment statements to describe the function of each subroutine, document the date it was last changed, and explain what is going on within code segments. These comments are extensive enough to serve fairly well as a programmer’s guide and are likely the reason a document like this one has not seemed critical to develop.

FVS code also has an internal debugging feature in the form of WRITE statements that output various program calculations and model controls. Outputs from these WRITE statements are included in the FVS main output file. This internal debug feature is turned on using the DEBUG keyword record. It can be activated for individual subroutines or globally throughout the model, and for individual cycles or all cycles. This feature produces a lot of output when turned on globally for all cycles. However, this feature is powerful enough that some programmers use it exclusively to find program bugs rather than implementing an off-the-shelf debugging product.

Subroutine INITRE processes model keyword records, including the DEBUG keyword record. INITRE calls subroutines DBPRSE or DBALL to schedule debug requests to the activity table. Subroutine DBCHK is used throughout program to check the activity table and see if the internal debug feature is active in an individual subroutine at the time the subroutine is called. A local logical variable, usually named DEBUG, is set to a value of “.TRUE.” when the internal DEBUG feature is on for that subroutine in that cycle or “.FALSE.” when it is not.

In some instances, the logical variable DEBUG is passed through a subroutine call list to a secondary subroutine. This occurs when the secondary subroutine is an integral part of the subroutine that called it, or when the secondary subroutine is called from multiple places for different purposes and you may want the debug output for only one of those places. An example of the first case is subroutine VARMRT that is variant-specific and only called from subroutine MORTS in the processing logic. However, if you are debugging mortality calculations, then it only makes sense that turning on debug for  subroutine MORTS also turns on debug in subroutine VARMRT so all mortality calculations are displayed. An example of the second case is subroutine FINDAG that estimates tree age from tree height and a site index curve for the individual species.  Subroutine FINDAG is called from various other subroutines. You may want debug output from FINDAG during model calibration in the projection initialization phase, but not during height growth estimation in the projection cycling phase.

Another important reason why the DEBUG variable is sometimes passed from one subroutine to another is that the subroutine DBCHK takes a lot of computer time. It is very inefficient to call it, for example, from within loops that are running over the entire tree list that might result in several thousand calls per growth cycle. It is much more efficient to call DBCHK at a higher level in the processing sequence and pass the value of DEBUG to subroutines that are called within a tree loop.

The NODEBUG keyword record can be used to turn the internal debug feature off. It is seldom, if ever, used in a single stand serial run. However, it may be useful in a multiple stand serial run. The DEBUG feature can be turned on globally for all stands, and then NODEBUG can be inserted for specific stands to omit those stands from producing debug output. Subroutine DBINIT is called for processing NODEBUG keyword record requests.

### Passing Data throughout the program

FVS makes heavy use of labeled COMMON blocks to make data available throughout the program. The COMMON block name gives an indication of the types of variables the COMMON block contains. For example, the PLOT labeled COMMON block contains plot level variables such as slope, aspect, elevation, and basal area per acre, while the ARRAYS labeled COMMON block contains individual tree arrays such as diameter at breast height, total tree height, and trees per acre that the tree record represents. Labeled COMMON blocks are the same across all geographic variants. An effort is made to provide variable definitions via comment statements within each labeled COMMON block for all variables contained in the labeled COMMON.

Many computer scientists discourage the use of COMMON blocks. However, FVS uses them for more than simple historical purposes and wholesale removal of them in favor of some other construct would break some model features. A key feature involves the ability to stop the program and restart it from the point where it left off (see section 8.0). COMMON blocks are like global structures in C; judicious use is often the only viable alternative to getting the job done.

Some variants utilize variables that are unique to the variant. The VARCOM labeled COMMON block was created to pass variant-specific variables. However, other even more variant-specific labeled COMMON blocks have been created over the years: CICOM is used in the CI variant; EMCOM is used in the EM variant; GGCOM is used in variants that use the GENGYM model logic; TWIGCOM is used in variants that use the Twigs model logic; and ORGANON is used in the two variants that use the ORGANON model logic (see section 9.0). These variant-specific COMMON blocks tend to be very small.

Global array dimensions and other controlling scalars are set in parameter statements in the PRGPRM, ESPARM, and other similar code segments. These code segments are variant-specific and set dimensions such as the total number of tree records allowed in the simulation, the number of species contained in the variant, and the FVS sequence numbers for which species will automatically regenerate (sprout) following harvesting.

FVS also makes extensive use of subroutine argument lists to pass arrays and scalars from one code segment to another. These are generally used where program control is only transferred from the calling subroutine to the called subroutine for a short calculation or task.

In recent years, an effort has been made to explicitly type all variables. However, some code segments, especially in the insect and disease extensions may still contain some implicitly typed arrays and scalars. Implicit typing is an old FORTRAN construct whereby variables with names that start with the letters I, J, K, L, M, or N (or in lowercase) are considered integers and other variables are 32-bit reals. Any time one of these subroutines is worked on, the change to explicit typing should be added and an IMPLICIT NONE directive added to the subroutine.

Two other techniques are used to cut down on storage space requirements and passing of coefficients. Limited use is still made of EQUIVALENCE statements although these are outdated and should be replaced with pointers or some other more modern FORTRAN code constructs.  In general, the EQUIVALENCE statements can be safely removed, but not in every case. They should be removed where possible.

There are several “work arrays” which reside in the WORKCM labeled COMMON block and are used to pass data from one part of the model to another, and then reused for the same purpose but with different data in a different part of the model. Some of these arrays are dimensioned by the maximum number of species the variant accommodates and some by the maximum number of tree records allowed. Usage of these arrays must be carefully documented in the COMMON block in which they reside to avoid corruption of the data they contain.

A unique 2-character alpha code identifies which variant is being run. For example the alpha code “IE” is used to identify the Inland Empire geographic variant. This alpha code is stored in the variable VARACD that is carried in the CONTRL.F77 labelled COMMON block.

### General Model Architecture

Three types of input data are needed by FVS: 1) data containing information communicating FVS parameter settings and what the user wants FVS to do, 2) data communicating stand-level information, and 3) data containing information about the individual tree inventory. The second and third type of information can be read directly out of a database, or contained in two external files called the keyword record file and tree data file. These two external files will be referred to throughout this document but keep in mind the data could easily come from a database instead. However, even when a database is used, the keyword record file is required and controls the basic input, even if it is brief. There is one exception. The stop and restart capability of FVS is discussed in section 8.0. When a restart file is used to start FVS from where it left off, a keyword record file is not used.

Users set projection parameters and communicate management activities to FVS through the use of keyword records. Keyword records containing parameter and stand-level information are handled differently than those indicating management activities. How FVS processes keyword records will be discussed in section 3.3.

Management activities can be scheduled by year, projection cycle, or by defining a condition using an IF-THEN-ENDIF keyword record sequence. Conceptually there is an activity schedule table inside FVS where each row corresponds to a particular management activity and the columns correspond to the parameters associated with that management activity including the year it is scheduled. As keyword records get processed in the projection initialization phase, activities will be posted to the activity schedule table. During the projection cycling phase stand conditions will be monitored and any management activities scheduled by condition will be posted to the activity schedule table if the condition is satisfied. Each projection cycle the activity schedule table is consulted to see if any management activities need to be done. Some activities may not get done for various reasons. Activities get tagged as “DONE”, “NOT DONE”, or “CANCELLED” depending upon their disposition (see section 3.3.1.3 for more information on this topic).

How FVS processes tree input data will be discussed in section 3.5. Data for individual tree records is kept in various arrays in the ARRAYS labeled COMMON block. These arrays get updated as the projection progresses through time and summarized across all tree records to calculate stand level statistics. For example, one key variable, PROB(i), where “i” is the tree record index, is the number of trees per acre that the tree record represents. This variable is used extensively throughout the model.

### Code Organization and Linking Considerations

There are about 25 different geographic variants of FVS either used or under development in the United States. An efficient source code system avoiding duplication cuts down on maintenance requirements and speeds up change implementation. For example, if an equation is changed in a subroutine that is used in all variants, it is more efficient to change it in one place and have that change implemented in all 25 variants rather than having to change it in all 25 variants. This is the motivation behind the FVS code storage structure shown in Appendix A.

Individual code segments are linked together to form an FVS executable program. In FVS nomenclature there is the base model and there are extensions to the base model. For each base model extension there is a code segment in the base model source directory containing all the external references needed by the base model for that extension. These are identifiable by the letters “EX” at the beginning of the subroutine name. For example, for the fire and fuels extension (FFE), there is a subroutine named EXFIRE in the base model source directory containing all the external references needed by the base model to run the FFE. To link an executable without any extensions, all these “EX” subroutines must be included in the link instructions. To include an extension, simply remove the corresponding EX subroutine in the link instructions and insert the code segment names making up the extension. Subroutine EXTREE, that is used to assign example trees to the output arrays, is currently the only “EX” named base model subroutine that is not a container of external references for a model extension.

With the code structure of FVS it is a simple matter to change some of the model limits specified in the PRGPRM code segments. For example, the default number of tree records allowed in FVS is limited to 3000. To change this, first change it in PRGPRM and then re-compile the source code and re-link the program executable. While this limit can be increased or decreased, it should not be reduced below about 1000 to maintain statistical properties of the model and because some of the work arrays dimensioned by this variable are used for other purposes. This fact may indeed be unfortunate and should be changed, but it is a current reality. Also, it should be kept as a multiple of 3 (e.g. 999 or 1002) to be consistent with the model’s record tripling process.

### Accessing Tree Records

FVS has a tree list that holds up to 3000 tree records (the default limit). The number of tree records in a simulation during any cycle can vary depending on the number of tree data records input, record tripling, harvesting, mortality, and regeneration. Knowing how to efficiently access the tree information is important for programming efficiency.

Tree record data is initially stored in tree data arrays in the order that the data was input. This order can change through one of the other FVS processes listed above. The main point being that the tree data is not stored in any kind of sorted order. The number of tree records in a simulation, at any point of the simulation, is carried in the variable ITRN stored in the CONTRL labeled COMMON block. An internal FVS sequence number is assigned to each tree record. These internal sequence numbers range from 1 to ITRN and indicate the storage index, or pointer, in the tree data arrays containing the information for that tree record. For example, if the internal sequence number is 5, the tree diameter represented by that tree record is in location DBH(5), the total tree height is in HT(5) and the trees per acre is in PROB(5).

In the computer code it is more efficient to loop over all tree records for some operations and over all tree records of a given species for other operations. For example, to compute quadratic mean diameter you just need to loop over all tree records in the stand, in any order, and get the sum of squared diameters and trees per acre. There aren’t any species-specific coefficients to access in that calculation. However, if you are in a growth projection loop it is more efficient to access species coefficients once and then loop through all the tree records of that species predicting growth than it would be to access species coefficients for each and every tree record as it is encountered.

Looping over all tree records is a simple matter. The looping just needs to take place from indices 1 to ITRN. The actual code might look something like the 10 lines shown below for computing quadratic mean diameter (QMD). Note that code is included to handle the case where there are no tree records (ITRN = 0), or where the number of trees per acre is too small to compute a reasonable QMD. For this example, the test for computing a reasonable QMD compares SUMTPA to 0.001; perhaps a different threshold should be used. However, comparing SUMTPA to exactly zero should be avoided.

QMD = 0.

IF (ITRN .GT. 0) THEN

SUMD2 = 0.

SUMTPA=0.

DO I=1,ITRN

SUMD2 = SUMD2 + DBH(I)*DBH(I)*PROB(I)

SUMTPA= SUMTPA + PROB(I)

ENDDO

IF (SUMTPA .GT. 0.001) QMD = SUMD2 / SUMTPA

ENDIF

There are three arrays in the ARRAYS labeled COMMON block that facilitate looping over all tree records, in individual species groups, or by size. These arrays also facilitate many FVS internal calculations that are dependent on tree size, such as a trees percentile ranking by some attribute.

The IND(i) array contains integer pointers, or indices, to locations in the tree data arrays containing information for a particular tree record. The IND(i) array is in sorted order by descending diameter. For example, if IND(20) = 1 then the tree record with information stored in the tree data arrays in location 20 is for the largest diameter tree in the stand.

The IND1(k) array is used to access tree data in species order. IND1(k) contains sectors such that each sector contains indices to the internal FVS sequence numbers for all records of a given species. A companion array, ISCT(i,j), is used to access the IND1(k) array. There are two elements in the ISCT(i,j) array for each species. ISCT(i,1) points to the first record in the sector of IND1(k) that is associated with species i; ISCT(i,2) points to the last record in the sector of IND1(k) that is associated with species i. If there are no records for species i, then ISCT(i,1) and ISCT(i,2) will contain zeroes. The actual code to access tree data in species order might look something like this (also notice an example of the internal debug feature near the end of this code segment):

C----------

C  BEGIN SPECIES LOOP

C----------

DO 20 ISPC=1,MAXSP

I1=ISCT(ISPC,1)

IF(I1.EQ.0) GO TO 20

I2=ISCT(ISPC,2)

CONSPP= DGCON(ISPC) + COR(ISPC) + 0.01*DGCCF(ISPC)*RELDEN

DGLDS= DGLD(ISPC)

DGBALS = DGBAL(ISPC)

DGCRS= DGCR(ISPC)

DGCRS2=DGCRSQ(ISPC)

DGDSQS=DGDSQ(ISPC)

DGDBLS=DGDBAL(ISPC)

C----------

C  BEGIN TREE LOOP WITHIN SPECIES LOOP

C----------

DO 10 I3=I1,I2

I=IND1(I3)

D=DIAM(I)

IF (D.LE.0.0) GOTO 10

ALD=ALOG(D)

CR=ICR(I)*0.01

BAL=(1.0 - (PCT(I)/100.)) * BA100

DDS=CONSPP + DGLDS*ALD + DGBALS*BAL + CR* (DGCRS +

&  CR*DGCRS2) +DGDSQS*D*D + DGDBLS*BAL/(ALOG(D+1.0))

IF(DDS.LT.-9.21) DDS=-9.21

WK2(I)=DDS

C----------

C  PRINT DEBUG INFORMATION, IF DESIRED

C----------

IF(DEBUG)THEN

WRITE(JOSTND,9001) I,ISPC,D,BAL,CR,RELDEN,BA,DDS

9001FORMAT(' IN DGF, I=',I4,',  ISPC=',I3,',  DBH=',F7.2,

&',  BAL=',F7.2,',  CR=',F7.4/

&5X,'CCF=',F9.3,',  BA=',F9.3,',   LN(DDS)=',F7.4)

ENDIF

C----------

C  END OF TREE LOOP

C----------

10  CONTINUE

C----------

C  END OF SPECIES LOOP

C----------

20  CONTINUE

## The Main FVS Routine

The main routine for the FVS model is appropriately called PROGRAM MAIN.  MAIN calls subroutine fvsSetCmdLine (the source code for this subroutine is part of the source code of subroutine CMDLINE) to retrieve any options that may, optionally, have been specified in the command that starts FVS (those may include the name of the keyword record file, the name of the restart file, or parameters that control stopping points (see section 8.0).  PROGRAM MAIN is very short and most programmers can ignore it. It calls one major subroutine, named FVS, which orchestrates all other subroutines, and it contains the only STOP statement in the program. In short, subroutine FVS contains what was once the MAIN program. This top-level organization was introduced in about 2010 to support the use of FVS as a shared library that is called by other upper-level programs (see section 8.0).

As part of its projection initialization phase, subroutine FVS calls subroutines to perform the following tasks:

check (again) for command line options,

check for return codes that may have been set at various stages,

check for restart codes causing the program to restart from a previously created stop point file if specified on the command line (see section 8.0),

open the key input and output files that will be required for the projection,

initialize parameters to their default condition,

process all keyword record requests,

set up the main projection cycling array,

initialize any files needed by extensions such as insect and disease models,

establish the initial species sort,

expand the tree data to a trees per acre basis based on the specified sample design,

calibrate internal equations to match the incoming tree data,

flag best trees for regeneration establishment model use,

compute initial tree record level variables such as volumes and crown width,

compute initial stand level variables such as basal area per acre,

compute the initial percentile distributions of various tree attributes,

assign example trees to the sample tree output arrays, compute cover statistics if the cover extension is being used,

compute a statistical description of the input data,

write any initial stand data that needs to be saved for output, visualization, or use with other programs.

As part of the projection cycling phase, subroutine FVS calls various subroutines to estimate tree growth and mortality, process management requests, establish regeneration, and write any stand data that needs to be saved for output, visualization, or use with other programs.

As part of the projection summarization phase, subroutine FVS calls various subroutines to produce the final output reports.

Subroutine FVS then checks to see if any more stands are being processed. If more stands are being processed then control branches back to the projection initialization phase for the next stand and the sequence is repeated. If this is not a multi-stand run, the run ends.

A logical variable, LSTART, has a value of “.TRUE.” during the projection initialization phase and “.FALSE.” when that phase is completed. This variable is used extensively during model calibration, discussed in section 3.6, to control program logic flow.

The differences in program flow for a parallel run will be discussed in section 8.0.

# Projection Initialization Phase

The FVS model must go through various steps and checks in preparation for a single stand growth projection. Model parameters and variables must be initialized to their default starting values. User model controls must be input and stored. Tree data (if any) must be input, any missing data values filled in, and the data expanded to a per-acre basis. Self-calibration of model equations to the input data needs to take place. Once this phase is completed FVS is calibrated to local stand conditions, knows what projection to make in terms of projection length, management actions, model output, and other user instructions, and has the tree data to make it. Upon completion of the projection initialization phase, tree data may not yet exist if this is a bare ground projection.

## Detailed Input and Output Array Specifications {-}

The following tables document the major arrays used in each phase of projection initialization:

### File Opening and I/O Management (Section 3.1) {-}

```{r section3-1-arrays, echo=FALSE}
file_arrays <- data.frame(
  Array_Name = c("IREAD", "JOSTND", "ISTDAT", "JOLIST", "JOSUM", "JOSUME", "JOSCRT", "JONEWF", "KOLIST", "JOCALB"),
  Common_Block = c("CONTRL", "CONTRL", "CONTRL", "CONTRL", "CONTRL", "ECON", "local", "local", "FVSSTDCM/local", "CONTRL"),
  Type = c("INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER", "INTEGER"),
  Direction = c("OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT", "OUTPUT"),
  Description = c(
    "Unit 15: Keyword record file",
    "Unit 16: Main FVS output file",
    "Unit 2: Tree data file",
    "Unit 3: Tree list output file (TREELIST)",
    "Unit 4: Summary statistics file (ECHOSUM)",
    "Unit 13: CHEAPO II / calibration stats file",
    "Unit 93: GENRPT scratch file for reports",
    "Unit 92: Permanent copy of GENRPT file",
    "Unit 30: FVSSTAND/National Cruise file",

  ),

      col.names = c("Array/Variable", "Common Block", "Type", "Direction", "Description"),

## Processing Sequence Diagrams {-}

The following diagrams illustrate the processing sequence for projection initialization:

### Overall Initialization Sequence {-}

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    PROJECTION INITIALIZATION                     │
│                      (FVS → INITRE)                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.1: File Opening and I/O Setup                  │
    │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────          │
    │  FVS → fvsSetCmdLine (CMDLINE)                          │
    │    → GENRPT (initialize multi-report scratch file)      │
    │    → FILOPN (open keyword file, output file)            │
    │      → MYOPEN/openIfClosed (file operations)            │
    │                                                           │
    │  Files opened:                                           │
    │    • Keyword file (unit IREAD=15)                        │
    │    • Output file (unit JOSTND=16)                        │
    │    • Scratch file (unit JOSCRT=93)                       │
    │  Other files opened as needed during run                 │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.2: Initialize Parameters                       │
    │  ──────────────────────────────────                     │
    │  INITRE → GRINIT (variant-specific defaults)            │
    │                                                           │
    │  Sets default values:                                    │
    │    • Species parameters (site index, SDI max)            │
    │    • Stand attributes (slope, aspect, elevation)         │
    │    • Control flags (LSTART=.TRUE., ICYC=0)              │
    │                                                           │
    │  INITRE → ... (keyword processing) ...                  │
    │         → SITSET (complete parameter initialization)    │
    │                                                           │
    │  Completes parameter values not set by user             │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.3: Process Keyword Records                      │
    │  ───────────────────────────────────                    │
    │  INITRE → KEYRDR (read each keyword)                    │
    │         → FNDKEY (find in TABLE array)                  │
    │                                                           │
    │  For each keyword type:                                  │
    │                                                           │
    │  ┌─ Immediate parameter setting (BAMAX, DEFECT, etc.)   │
    │  │   INITRE stores values directly                       │
    │  │                                                        │
    │  ┌─ Extension transfer (FMIN, COMPUTE, DATABASE, etc.)  │
    │  │   INITRE → Extension processor until END             │
    │  │                                                        │
    │  └─ Scheduled activities (THIN, PLANT, TREELIST, etc.)  │
    │      INITRE → KEYRDR → OPNEW/OPNEWC                     │
    │                      → Post to activity schedule        │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.4: Process Event Monitor                        │
    │  ──────────────────────────────────                     │
    │  INITRE → EVIF (IF keyword)                             │
    │         → EVCOMP → ALGCMP (compile logical expression)  │
    │         → EVTHEN (THEN keyword)                         │
    │         → EVEND (ENDIF keyword)                         │
    │                                                           │
    │  INITRE → EVUSRV (COMPUTE keyword)                      │
    │         → ALGEXP (read expression)                      │
    │         → ALGCMP (compile expression)                   │
    │         → OPNEW (schedule, option code 33)              │
    │                                                           │
    │  Results stored in OPCOM: IVENTS(i,j), IEVACT(i,j)     │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.5: Read Stand and Tree Data                    │
    │  ─────────────────────────────────────                  │
    │  Decision point: Data source?                            │
    │    ┌─ Database: INITRE → DBSIN                          │
    │    │              → DBSOPEN (establish connection)       │
    │    │              → DBSSTANDIN (STANDSQL keyword)        │
    │    │              → DBSTREESIN → INTREE (TREESQL)        │
    │    │                                                      │
    │    └─ Flat file: INITRE → INTREE (at TREEDATA/PROCESS)  │
    │                                                           │
    │  INTREE processing:                                      │
    │    → Read tree records → arrays: DBH(), HT(), PROB(),  │
    │      ISP(), ICR(), IMC(), NORMHT()                      │
    │    → DAMCDS → BASDAM (process damage codes)             │
    │    → LNKCHN (establish sort sequence)                   │
    │    → Store in ARRAYS common block                       │
    │                                                           │
    │  INITRE → DAMPRO (process damage for extensions)        │
    │         → TRESOR (match tree IDs to indices)            │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.6: Model Calibration and Setup                 │
    │  ────────────────────────────────────────               │
    │  FVS → SETUP (species sort: IND1, ISCT arrays)          │
    │      → NOTRE (expand to per-acre basis)                 │
    │      → Extension initializations                         │
    │      → OPCSET (set option pointers, ICYC=1)             │
    │      → SDICLS (compute max SDI for calibration)         │
    │      → CRATET ──────────────────────────────────┐       │
    │                                                   │       │
    │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┘      │
    │  │ CRATET: Model Calibration Sequence                   │
    │  │ ──────────────────────────────────                   │
    │  │ 1. Calculate site/stand variables:                   │
    │  │    → MBACAL (identify site species)                  │
    │  │    → MAICAL (compute mean annual increment)          │
    │  │    → RCON (aggregate site-level terms)               │
    │  │       → DGCONS, HTCONS, REGCON, MORCON, CRCONS      │
    │  │    → DENSE (LBKDEN=.TRUE., backdate stand)           │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  │ 2. Process mortality records (history=7,9):          │
    │  │    → Identify non-projectable trees                  │
    │  │    → Realign IND1, ISCT sort pointers                │
    │  │    → Dead tree data remains in bottom of arrays      │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  │ 3. Calibrate height-diameter equation:               │
    │  │    → Adjust B1 intercept if ≥3 measured heights      │
    │  │    → Dub missing heights for live and dead trees     │
    │  │    → Formula: HT = 4.5 + exp(B1 + B2/(DBH+1))       │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  │ 4. Add dead trees to snag list:                      │
    │  │    → FMSSEE (fire/fuels extension)                   │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  │ 5. Dub missing crown ratios:                         │
    │  │    → CROWN → DUBSCR (small trees, dead trees)        │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  │ 6. Calibrate growth equations:                       │
    │  │    → AVHT40 (if needed for growth equations)         │
    │  │    → DGDRIV (large-tree diameter growth)             │
    │  │       → DGF (predict DG for all trees)               │
    │  │       → Store ln(BAI) in WK2()                       │
    │  │       → Calculate scale factors (median obs/pred)    │
    │  │    → FINDAG (estimate tree ages if needed)           │
    │  │    → REGENT (small-tree height growth)               │
    │  │       → Calculate scale factors                      │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  │ 7. Final calibration steps:                          │
    │  │    → PCTILE, DIST, COMP, DENSE (initial stand)       │
    │  │    → SDICHK (verify SDI ≤ SDI_max)                   │
    │  │                                                       │
    │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
    │                                                           │
    │  Calibration complete: growth functions scaled to data  │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  Phase 3.7: Final Initialization Tasks                  │
    │  ───────────────────────────────────────────            │
    │  FVS → ESFLTR (regeneration: overstory/best trees)      │
    │      → Set ICYC = 0 (inventory time)                    │
    │      → CWIDTH → CWCALC (estimate crown widths)          │
    │      → VOLS (compute initial volumes)                   │
    │      → PCTILE, DIST (volume distributions)              │
    │      → EXTREE (assign example trees to INS array)       │
    │      → Cover extension (if active)                       │
    │      → STATS (plot statistics if requested)             │
    │                                                           │
    │  Write initial output:                                   │
    │      → DISPLY (stand statistics to output file)          │
    │      → MISPRT (mistletoe info if present)                │
    │      → PRTRLS (cycle 0 tree list if requested)           │
    │      → FVSSTD (FVSSTAND file if requested)               │
    │      → NATCRZ (National Cruise file if requested)        │
    │                                                           │
    │  Purge dead trees:                                       │
    │      → Reset IREC2 = MAXTP1 (MAXTRE+1)                  │
    │      → Frees bottom of arrays for live tree storage     │
    │                                                           │
    │  Initialize extensions:                                  │
    │      → RDMN1, RDPR (root disease)                        │
    │      → BRSETP, BRPR (blister rust)                       │
    │                                                           │
    │  Final flag:                                             │
    │      → Set LSTART = .FALSE. (init complete)             │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                ┌─────────────────────────┐
                │  INITIALIZATION COMPLETE │
                │  Ready for Cycle 1       │
                │  (Projection Cycling)    │
                └─────────────────────────┘
```

### Keyword Processing Detail (Section 3.3) {-}

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            KEYWORD RECORD PROCESSING FLOW (INITRE)               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                     ┌────────────────┐
                     │  KEYRDR        │
                     │  Read keyword  │
                     └────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
                     ┌────────────────┐
                     │  FNDKEY        │
                     │  Find in TABLE │
                     └────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
        ┌─────────────────────┴──────────────────────┐
        │                     │                       │
        ▼                     ▼                       ▼
┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────┐
│ Type 1:      │    │ Type 2:          │    │ Type 3:           │
│ Immediate    │    │ Transfer Control │    │ Scheduled         │
│ Parameter    │    │ to Extension     │    │ Activity          │
└──────────────┘    └──────────────────┘    └───────────────────┘
        │                     │                       │
        ▼                     ▼                       ▼
┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐    ┌───────────────────┐
│ Examples:    │    │ Examples:        │    │ Examples:         │
│ • BAMAX      │    │ • COMPUTE → EVUSRV│   │ • THIN___         │
│ • DEFECT     │    │ • FMIN → FMIN    │    │ • PLANT           │
│ • CWEQN      │    │ • DATABASE→DBSIN │    │ • TREELIST        │
│ • STDINFO    │    │ • MISIN → MISIN  │    │ • FIXDG           │
│              │    │ (until END)      │    │ • MORTMULT        │
└──────────────┘    └──────────────────┘    └───────────────────┘
        │                     │                       │
        ▼                     ▼                       │
┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────────┐             │
│ Store values │    │ Extension        │             │
│ in variables │    │ processes own    │             │
│ or arrays    │    │ keywords until   │             │
│              │    │ END encountered  │             │
└──────────────┘    └──────────────────┘             │
                              │                       │
                              └───────────────────────┘
                                          │
                    ┌─────────────────────┴────────────────┐
                    │                                      │
                    ▼                                      ▼
          ┌──────────────────┐                  ┌──────────────────┐
          │ Non-PARMS format │                  │ PARMS format     │
          └──────────────────┘                  └──────────────────┘
                    │                                      │
                    ▼                                      ▼
          ┌──────────────────┐                  ┌──────────────────┐
          │ Check parameters │                  │ No parameter     │
          │ KEYRDR           │                  │ checking         │
          └──────────────────┘                  └──────────────────┘
                    │                                      │
                    ▼                                      ▼
          ┌──────────────────┐                  ┌──────────────────┐
          │ OPNEW            │                  │ OPNEWC           │
          │ Post to activity │                  │ → ALGCMP         │
          │ schedule         │                  │ Compile PARMS    │
          │                  │                  │ expressions      │
          └──────────────────┘                  └──────────────────┘
                    │                                      │
                    └──────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                   ▼
                         ┌──────────────────┐
                         │ Activity stored  │
                         │ in schedule with │
                         │ unique option    │
                         │ code (IACTK)     │
                         └──────────────────┘
                                   │
                                   ▼
                    ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                    │ Retrieved later in cycle by: │
                    │ OPFIND → OPGET → OPDONE      │
                    │                              │
                    │ Status: DONE / NOT DONE /    │
                    │         DELETED OR CANCELLED │
                    └──────────────────────────────┘
```

### Tree Data Input Processing (Section 3.5) {-}

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    TREE DATA INPUT PROCESSING                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
          ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
          │                                       │
          ▼                                       ▼
┌─────────────────────┐              ┌─────────────────────┐
│  DATABASE Keyword   │              │  Flat File Input    │
│  (DBSIN called)     │              │  (INTREE called at  │
│                     │              │   TREEDATA/PROCESS) │
└─────────────────────┘              └─────────────────────┘
          │                                       │
          ▼                                       │
┌─────────────────────┐                          │
│  DBSOPEN            │                          │
│  Establish DB       │                          │
│  connection         │                          │
└─────────────────────┘                          │
          │                                       │
          ▼                                       │
┌─────────────────────┐                          │
│  STANDSQL keyword?  │                          │
│  → DBSSTANDIN       │                          │
│  (SQL query for     │                          │
│   stand params)     │                          │
└─────────────────────┘                          │
          │                                       │
